analysis:
Examined the docs update (docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md), the new optional `stopsAsked` counter in ClusterSetupRecord (ClusterSetupWizardStore.swift head line 134), and the new `stopsBefore` request field plus `stopsAsked` status field in ClusterControlLeadership.swift (patch hunks near lines 828-836 and 869-878). The changes are additive and optional Codable fields (Int?), decoded under the existing 64 KiB bounded, owner-only record read and the schema check. Old records decode with nil. The setup record is documented as never an approval, and the counter only affects whether a follower screen ends its wait on a stop, or whether the leader skips a `serve`. Neither feeds attestation, App Attest authorization, encryption keys, the coordinator wire or the prompt/cache paths (TB-002, TB-011, T-041 are not affected).

Residual question for integration: `stopsBefore` is carried in a control request from the peer Mac. It is only consumed by a leader-side `serve` guard (`OnboardingLive.localServe(unlessStoppedSince:)`), which is not in the supplied source. A paired peer can already issue stop and serve, so a forged value adds no apparent new authority. The only effect would be that the leader declines to serve, which is a limited availability effect inside an already-authenticated pairing. The control channel's peer authentication, and the exact comparison and overflow handling of the counter (for example Int increment, or nil versus 0 on an older leader), cannot be verified from this batch. The doc also removes the 20-second 'stayed stopped' heuristic in favour of an explicit counter, which is a behavioral improvement. No regression is identified. No concrete security-relevant defect is supported by the visible lines.
